# Third-party notices

Conservative union of locked normal dependencies for the macOS ARM64 and Linux ARM64 client/service. Not every dependency is present in every artifact. Workspace code is MIT; third-party terms below remain applicable. Build tools, test-only dependencies and operating system components are not bundled in the binary archives.

Cargo.lock SHA256: `f44db5d7bf3eab30cba8d1bd79ac389509ba962d8309ab96fa8b2d9bda526356`. Vendored nfsserve is modified; its upstream license and patch provenance are retained below. Full texts are intentionally repeated where upstream supplies them.

## objc2-core-foundation-0.3.2

Declared license: Zlib OR Apache-2.0 OR MIT

Exact upstream: https://github.com/madsmtm/objc2/tree/7b1abfd750a2cacaea71d6a56ecfb83cb7de560b ; packaged manifest byte-matched to this revision. This upstream notice supplies no crate-specific copyright holder; none is invented here. The referenced MIT option is used for these two crates. Upstream Apple SDK caveat is reproduced without alteration or a compatibility conclusion.

### Upstream LICENSE.md

SHA256: `7f976f7e9cb2d87df7230606feb932c3f21ac0e664045a775b600046ff850c54`

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~text
# License

The licensing of these crates is a bit complicated:
- The crates `objc2`, `block2`, `objc2-foundation` and `objc2-encode` are
  [currently][#23] licensed under [the MIT license][MIT].
- All other crates are trio-licensed under the [Zlib], [Apache-2.0] or [MIT]
  license, at your option.

Furthermore, the crates are (usually automatically) derived from Apple SDKs,
and that may have implications for licensing, see below for details.

[#23]: https://github.com/madsmtm/objc2/issues/23
[MIT]: https://opensource.org/license/MIT
[Zlib]: https://zlib.net/zlib_license.html
[Apache-2.0]: https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0


## Apple SDKs

These crates are derived from Apple SDKs shipped with Xcode. You can obtain a
copy of the Xcode license at:

https://www.apple.com/legal/sla/docs/xcode.pdf

Or by typing `xcodebuild -license` in your terminal.

From reading the license, it is unclear whether distributing derived works
such as these crates are allowed?

But in any case, to practically use these crates, you will have to link, and
that only works when you have the correct Xcode SDK available to provide the
required `.tbd` files, which is why we choose to still use the normal SPDX
identifiers in the crates (Xcode is required to use the crates, and when using
Xcode you have already agreed to the Xcode license).
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

## nfsserve-0.11.0

Vendored modification provenance (source is modified from the recorded baseline).

### vendor/README.md

SHA256: `91036ba357cb36856383ca5020a97a186f35b792fc64e394c8dce16b6dbb2dc0`

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~text
# Local nfsserve 0.11.0 permission patch

`nfsserve-0.11.0/` is the exact published crate with only the changes in `nfsserve-access.patch`. The upstream BSD-3-Clause LICENSE is unchanged. `nfsserve-0.11.0-baseline.json` records every original file SHA-256, upstream VCS metadata, and the original crates.io archive SHA-256:

`ef1424b6d88c60a091931392970999ea3ceab132d968e6a5545c770fad5b97d7`

The archive checksum was verified against both the cached published archive and the original root Cargo.lock before adding the local path patch. No Cargo registry source/cache was modified. Root Cargo.lock now resolves the local path; the Linux Docker build explicitly copies vendor/.

The small patch adds a fail-closed `NFSFileSystem::access` policy hook, delegates ACCESS to it, retains the readonly mutation mask while permitting authorized EXECUTE, and omits READDIRPLUS child attributes/handles when authorized GETATTR fails. This avoids bypassing missing directory search permissions through prefetched metadata. RFC1813 permits the optional attributes/handle to be absent. The Magus FS0 adapter supplies the fixed-principal policy and checks GETATTR ancestors; the hook does not introduce request identity, authentication or a multi-user model.

Upstream readonly ACCESS previously returned READ|LOOKUP for every object, rejecting legitimate executable files and advertising search on unsearchable directories. Writable ACCESS echoed all request bits, including executable permission on mode0644. Merely changing the capability flag was therefore unsafe. Native and raw RPC regression evidence is retained in the Task2 report; tests/fs0/test_nfs.py covers masks, mode changes, forged credentials/handles, metadata omission and readonly mutation denial.

Maintenance cost: updates require rebasing this small patch, re-verifying the archive and file baselines, and rerunning both native permission/cleanup checks and Linux build/tests. The dependency is not a public fork or general NFS security qualification. No additional protocol/namespace/history engine is included. Inspect the patch rather than treating the entire vendored crate as newly authored code.

To audit, reverse-apply the patch to a temporary copy of the vendored directory and compare every file against the baseline checksums. The focused vendor regression performs this operation without touching the Cargo registry or working copy.

FS1 adds one defaulted `mkdir_with_attrs` hook and passes the already-decoded MKDIR sattr3 through it. Existing implementations still call their original mkdir; the durable adapter validates requested mode/ownership/size/times before creation. This prevents silently creating0755 for every requested directory mode. Upstream archive/license and baseline hashes remain unchanged; the complete patch still reconstructs them exactly.

FS1 also adds a defaulted `remove_directory` hook, preserving legacy `remove` behavior while distinguishing RMDIR in the dispatcher. The durable adapter validates target type under its serialized operation lock before the shared parent-authorized unlink. Wire regressions require REMOVE(directory)=ISDIR and RMDIR(file)=NOTDIR, with both targets unchanged. No unrelated dependency behavior or upstream checksum changes are included.
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

### vendor/nfsserve-access.patch

SHA256: `9b2a0b2be8bb9721b122cc79349454adfda042ce6b1154bd9c9ac2bba1b01171`

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~text
--- a/src/nfs_handlers.rs
+++ b/src/nfs_handlers.rs
@@ -147 +147 @@
-        NFSProgram::NFSPROC3_RMDIR => nfsproc3_remove(xid, input, output, context).await?,
+        NFSProgram::NFSPROC3_RMDIR => nfsproc3_remove_kind(xid, input, output, context, true).await?,
@@ -519 +519,10 @@
-    // TODO better checks here
+    access = match context.vfs.access(id, access).await {
+        Ok(allowed) => access & allowed,
+        Err(stat) => {
+            make_success_reply(xid).serialize(output)?;
+            stat.serialize(output)?;
+            obj_attr.serialize(output)?;
+            return Ok(());
+        },
+    };
+    // Read-only still permits execution; mutation rights remain protocol-masked.
@@ -521 +530 @@
-        access &= ACCESS3_READ | ACCESS3_LOOKUP;
+        access &= ACCESS3_READ | ACCESS3_LOOKUP | ACCESS3_EXECUTE;
@@ -890,2 +899,7 @@
-                let obj_attr = entry.attr;
-                let handle = nfs::post_op_fh3::handle(context.vfs.id_to_fh(entry.fileid));
+                // Names may be readable without permission to search this directory.
+                // RFC 1813 allows omitted child attributes and handles in READDIRPLUS.
+                let (obj_attr, handle) = match context.vfs.getattr(entry.fileid).await {
+                    Ok(attr) => (nfs::post_op_attr::attributes(attr),
+                                 nfs::post_op_fh3::handle(context.vfs.id_to_fh(entry.fileid))),
+                    Err(_) => (nfs::post_op_attr::Void, nfs::post_op_fh3::Void),
+                };
@@ -897 +911 @@
-                    name_attributes: nfs::post_op_attr::attributes(obj_attr),
+                    name_attributes: obj_attr,
@@ -1562,0 +1577,10 @@
+    nfsproc3_remove_kind(xid, input, output, context, false).await
+}
+
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
